DEFECT 1, CORRECTNESS, packages/data-model/dataverse-client.js encodeValue(): it encodes NOTHING. The regex /[A-Za-z0-9\-_~!'()*,\s]/g matches only the SAFE characters and the callback returns them unchanged, so every unsafe character passes through untouched - the opposite of the comment above it, which claims 'Everything else is percent-encoded'. PROVEN by running it: 'a&b=c#d' -> 'a&b=c#d' and 'x%20y' -> 'x%20y'. Any $filter value containing & # + or % therefore corrupts the query string or injects extra OData options. Add a unit test with & # + % and a space in one value. Git therefore classifies the file as BINARY - `gh pr diff` prints 'Binary files differ' and the test is unreviewable in any diff, now and forever. The file is otherwise valid UTF-8 (18,200 bytes, 437 LF, zero CR, so the CRLF discipline held). FIX: write the separator as the \0 escape (or any printable sentinel such as '\u0001' or '::') so the file stays text; confirm with `git diff --stat` that it reports line counts, not 'Bin'.
